Massachusetts hosts two tracked data center facilities, both concentrated in the greater Boston area, and the dataset records zero megawatts of capacity for either one.

The two facilities, CoreSite BO1 in Somerville and Markley Data Center in Middlesex County, sit within roughly 30 kilometers of each other. That geographic clustering is consistent with the Boston metro serving as the state's primary colocation market, but the data does not explain why capacity figures are absent. A zero total could mean the power draw was not reported, not yet measured, or genuinely negligible at the time of generation.

What the data cannot say is whether these facilities support AI workloads, what their physical footprint is, or how they connect to the regional grid. For readers tracking the compute-to-power chain, Massachusetts appears as a thin entry: two named locations, no confirmed megawatts, and no basis for comparing the state to larger data center markets.
